claims.explanation: Ouabain kills cancer cells by binding and inhibiting the Na+/K+-ATPase (ATP1A1), and selectivity likely reflects dependence on ATP1A1-mediated ion transport and downstream HIF-1alpha signaling. Lines with high ATP1A1 expression or HIF-1 pathway activation are expected to be more sensitive, while those with low pump dependence or compensatory survival signaling are protected. TP53 mutation is common across both sensitive and resistant lines and is not a strong discriminator.

features.basis: direct drug target; higher expression increases ouabain binding and pump inhibition
cardiac glycosides inhibit HIF-1alpha synthesis; HIF-1-dependent lines are more sensitive
beta-subunit required for functional Na/K-ATPase; expression supports ouabain-sensitive pump
alpha2 isoform has lower ouabain affinity than alpha1 and may sustain ion homeostasis
alpha3 isoform differs in ouabain sensitivity and may compensate for alpha1 inhibition
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via HIF-1 or ion transport dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines appear among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven ion transport dependence
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and is enriched in sensitive lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and appears in several sensitive lines
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and colorectal lines are enriched among resistant lines
TP53 mutation is common in both groups and not discriminatory; listed only to note lack of selectivity
